entries.nuMessage: Bad value “5; href=http://example.com” for attribute “content” on element “meta”: Expected a space character, but saw “h” instead.
entries.reason: HTML LS §4.2.5.3 clause 3.3 accepts the URL part as either 'URL=<url>' or a bare 'valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces'. `href=http://example.com` is itself a parseable relative-URL string (the '=' is a valid path code point per URL LS), so it matches the bare-URL alternative and the content value is spec-conformant. nu-validator treats only the literal 'URL=' keyword path as valid; that is stricter than HTML LS.

entries.nuMessage: Bad value “5;url=http://example.com” for attribute “content” on element “meta”: Expected a space character, but saw “u” instead.
entries.reason: HTML LS §4.2.5.3 clause 3.2 — 'Optionally, ASCII whitespace.' — makes the whitespace after the ';' or ',' separator optional. `5;url=http://example.com` matches the grammar and is spec-conformant. nu-validator requires a space after the separator; that is stricter than HTML LS.

entries.nuMessage: Bad value “5; url='http://example.com'” for attribute “content” on element “meta”: Expected an unquoted URL.
entries.reason: HTML LS §4.2.5.3 clause 3.3 requires a 'valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces'. U+0027 (') is a URL code point (URL LS §3.5), so `'http://example.com'` is a parseable relative-URL string — it serialises to a path segment containing the quotes. The content value is spec-conformant. nu-validator rejects single-quoted URLs by convention; that is stricter than HTML LS.

HTML LS §4.8.7: 'Either the data attribute or the type attribute must be specified.' The fixture has `<object type=…>` (type-only) which the spec accepts. nu-validator reports `data` as unconditionally required, which is stricter than HTML LS — markuplint's existing requiredEither on data/type already implements the spec contract.

entries.nuMessage: `<script type=importmap>` scope key fails nu's looks-like-URL check (`scope1_not_url`).
entries.reason: HTML LS § Sorting and normalizing scopes step 2 URL-parses scopePrefix *with* baseURL. Relative strings like `scope1_not_url` parse successfully against any base, so step 3's URL-parse-failure warning never fires; the resulting scope simply applies to `<base>/scope1_not_url`. nu-validator additionally requires the key to look URL-like (scheme or `/`/`./`/`../`), which is stricter than the spec. The `script-content` rule deliberately follows the spec letter and does not flag this case.

entries.nuMessage: A table row was 3 columns wide and exceeded the column count established using column markup (2).
entries.reason: HTML LS §4.9.12.1 *Algorithm for processing rows* Step 7: 'If xcurrent is equal to xwidth, then increase xwidth by 1.' xwidth grows automatically when a row has more cells than the current column count established by column markup. There is no spec rule that row width must not exceed column markup width — extra columns are silently created. After xwidth growth every column in this row has an anchor cell, so Step 20 (no-anchor) is also not violated. nu-validator's 'exceeded the column count established using column markup' is heuristic over-detection.

entries.nuMessage: Bad value “allow-scripts allow-same-origin” for attribute “sandbox” on element “iframe”: Setting both “allow-scripts” and “allow-same-origin” is not recommended, because it effectively enables an embedded page to break out of all sandboxing.
entries.reason:
HTML LS § the iframe element renders this advisory as `

`: 'Setting both the allow-scripts and allow-same-origin keywords together when the embedded page has the same origin as the page containing the iframe allows the embedded page to simply remove the sandbox attribute and then reload itself, effectively breaking out of the sandbox altogether.' The `

` container marks the paragraph as a non-normative advisory (contrast with `must` / `must not` prose in the same section). The two-keyword pair is spec-conformant; nu-validator escalates the advisory to an error. markuplint follows the letter of the spec here and does not flag it.

entries.nuMessage: Element “input” with attribute “type” whose value is “button” must have non-empty attribute “value”.
entries.reason: HTML LS §4.10.5.1.21 Button state (type=button) has two adjacent sentences: (i) 'A label for the button must be provided in the value attribute, though it may be the empty string.' — a locus rule constraining *where* the label goes when the author does provide one, not a hard requirement that the value attribute be present; (ii) 'If the element has a value attribute, the button's label must be the value of that attribute; otherwise, it must be the empty string.' — a UA-side fallback that defines a spec-conformant behaviour for the missing-attribute case. The existence of the UA fallback in (ii) means the spec treats a missing value attribute as a supported state, not as a `must`-violation of (i). The `input-button-non-empty-value` rule reads the two sentences the same way and deliberately fires only on the explicit `value=""` case (spec-cited rationale in the rule's JSDoc and README; design decision recorded in commit 3096626bc `fix(rules): tighten new conformance rules from QA review`, section 3). nu-validator's Assertions.java enforces both the missing and the empty-string case; markuplint follows the spec letter on missing.

entries.nuMessage: Bad value “default-src 'self'; invalid-directive 'none'” for attribute “content” on element “meta”: Unrecognized directive invalid-directive
entries.reason: deferred-CSP (#3942). markuplint's tracked spec scope per `.claude/skills/bench-triage/SKILL.md` is HTML Living Standard + WAI-ARIA + URL Living Standard. The Content Security Policy Level 3 grammar (directive names, source expressions, ASCII-only body) is a separate W3C specification and is not currently validated. `packages/@markuplint/html-spec/src/spec.meta.jsonc` documents this explicitly: `Other http-equiv values (default-style, content-security-policy) and 'name' / 'itemprop' fall through to "Any" at runtime`. CSP3 §Directives (https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/#framework-directives): "A directive is a name / value pair which declares a policy for a particular type of behavior." The set of recognized directive names is enumerated in the CSP3 directive registry (§6 Content Security Policy Directives); `invalid-directive` is not registered, so nu-validator is spec-correct — markuplint simply does not track that spec. Filename suffix `-haswarn` notwithstanding, the actual nu message carries `type: error`, so the fixture participates in bench verdict computation.

entries.nuMessage: Bad value “default-src 'invalid-keyword'” for attribute “content” on element “meta”: Unrecognized source-expression 'invalid-keyword'
entries.reason: deferred-CSP (#3942). markuplint's tracked spec scope per `.claude/skills/bench-triage/SKILL.md` is HTML Living Standard + WAI-ARIA + URL Living Standard. CSP3 §6.7.2 Serialized Source List (https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/#framework-directive-source-list) ABNF: `source-expression = scheme-source / host-source / keyword-source / 'self' / 'unsafe-inline' / 'unsafe-eval' / 'strict-dynamic' / 'unsafe-hashes' / 'report-sample' / 'unsafe-allow-redirects' / nonce-source / hash-source`. `'invalid-keyword'` is a quoted string that matches none of the listed alternatives, so nu-validator is spec-correct — markuplint does not currently track that spec. See the `spec.meta.jsonc` fall-through comment for why `content` under `[http-equiv='content-security-policy' i]` is `Any`.

entries.nuMessage: Bad value “default-src 'self'; img-src https://例え.com” for attribute “content” on element “meta”: Content Security Policy must contain only ASCII characters.
entries.reason: deferred-CSP (#3942). markuplint's tracked spec scope per `.claude/skills/bench-triage/SKILL.md` is HTML Living Standard + WAI-ARIA + URL Living Standard. CSP3 §4.1 Policies (https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/#framework-policy) ABNF: `serialized-policy = serialized-directive *( OWS ';' [ OWS serialized-directive ] )` and `serialized-directive = directive-name [ RWS directive-value ]`. Both `directive-name` and `directive-value` are defined via HTTP header-field grammar productions restricted to VCHAR / SP / HTAB, so the serialized policy is ASCII by construction. Non-ASCII host authorities like `例え.com` violate this constraint, so nu-validator is spec-correct — markuplint does not currently track that spec. See the `spec.meta.jsonc` fall-through comment for why `content` under `[http-equiv='content-security-policy' i]` is `Any`.

deferred-CSS (#3946). markuplint's tracked spec scope per `.claude/skills/bench-triage/SKILL.md` is HTML Living Standard + WAI-ARIA + URL Living Standard. CSS syntax and the property registry are governed by CSS specifications (CSS Syntax Level 3, CSS Values and Units, and the individual property specifications hosted by W3C CSSWG), not by HTML LS. `colr` is not a registered CSS property (see the CSS property registry at https://www.w3.org/Style/CSS/all-properties.en.html — the closest tokens are `color` and the color-adjacent family, none of which spell `colr`), so nu-validator is spec-correct. markuplint currently does not validate CSS content inside `<style>` or `[style]`. Parallel deferred spec: #3942 (deferred-CSP).

patterns.messageContains: Fragment is not allowed for data: URIs according to RFC 2397
patterns.reason: WHATWG URL Living Standard supersedes RFC 2397. Per URL LS §4.3, 'A valid URL string must be either a relative-URL-with-fragment string or an absolute-URL-with-fragment string.' An absolute-URL-with-fragment string is 'an absolute-URL string, optionally followed by U+0023 (#) and a URL-fragment string.' Since 'data' is a non-special scheme, 'data:<body>#<fragment>' matches this grammar and is a valid URL string. HTML conformance (which requires a valid URL string) is therefore satisfied.
